definitions.explanation: A fluid-filled bubble on the skin caused by friction, heat, or repeated pressure. Commonly occurs on the hands from gripping tools or on the feet from walking or ill-fitting shoes.
A thickened, hardened area of skin that develops from repeated friction or pressure over time.

examples.english: I got a blister on my hand.

notes:
Usually written in katakana (マメ) or hiragana (まめ) to distinguish from ⟦{豆|まめ}→豆：03738_mame⟧ (bean). The connection is that blisters and calluses resemble small beans in shape.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マメ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧: to get a blister/callus
- マメ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦つぶれる→つぶる：29078_tsuburu⟧: a blister bursts
- マメ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{硬|かた}く→硬い：01116_katai⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: a callus hardens
- ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧マメ: blister/callus on the hand

USAGE:
The distinction between blister (fluid-filled) and callus (hardened skin) depends on context. Fresh マメ from short-term friction are blisters; long-term マメ from repeated activity become calluses.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {水膨|みずぶく}れ: water blister — specifically a fluid-filled blister
- たこ: callus; corn — hardened skin, often on feet
